findings.finding: Publisher score p.13 shows upper-voice treble-clef writing, articulated exchanges between the two groups, and the exposed Chorale.
Tarantella p.15 is Allegro con fuoco, dotted quarter about 132: brisk slurred eighth-note figures, upper-register first viola, and coordinated accents across eight parts.

grade.basis: Score-preview assessment: the leading viola needs secure upper-register facility and fast compound-time articulation; eight-way rhythmic precision and chorale tuning bring the whole work to pre-diploma level. The material seen is energetic rather than extreme virtuosity.

grade.basis: Exact-arrangement preview plus repertoire expertise in Passione amorosa: the principal bass writing retains soloistic high-register, thumb-position demands and later brilliant display. Supporting basses must maintain a light texture underneath unusually exposed solo bass intonation. Professional level, with bass 2 also demanding; not graded from the easier accompaniment alone.

findings.finding: First violin part, Peters plate 7943, pp.1–2: Adagio followed by Allegro molto; repeated double stops, rapid upper-register runs, chromatic writing, wide register changes and exposed lyrical high-position playing.

grade.basis: Direct first-part inspection: sustained virtuoso passagework and double-stop accuracy at Allegro molto require professional command. The three-violin texture adds exposed tuning and articulation coordination, but the inspected writing does not justify extreme-virtuoso level.

findings.finding: Publisher identifies an eight-violin, eight-minute work and describes its motoric virtuosity and kinetic energy.

grade.basis: Repertoire-expertise assessment of Gran Turismo, supported by publisher characterization; the supplied NSO PDF is a concert programme, not a score. Its sustained racing passagework, rapid exchanges and exact eight-player coordination demand a virtuoso ensemble, above the professional baseline. No specific unseen score device is asserted.

findings.finding: Kimura BC4131 opening page shows the first violin carrying continuous decorated semiquaver figuration over three independent accompanying parts.
Page 8 shows the richly ornamented slow-movement solo line with long slurred chromatic runs and trills, followed by the Presto opening.

grade.basis: Exact-version score previews include both the slow-movement close and finale opening. First violin agility, ornament control and long-phrase bow planning exceed the Bach Double anchor; coordinated contrapuntal articulation and balance put the work at pre-diploma level. The keyboard original was not used as an instrumental difficulty proxy.

findings.finding: Publisher first page shows the Cucaraccia at quarter 144, interlocking pizzicato patterns, arco changes and an exposed first-viola solo.
Publisher second preview, score p.6, shows imitative entries, chromatic accidentals and a coordinated crescendo and ritardando to the close.

grade.basis: Direct previews: individual technique is advanced, with the top viola’s solo line the clearest local peak. Tight interlocking pizzicato timing, matching articulation and independent contrapuntal tuning raise the ensemble assessment to pre-diploma; the short duration limits the stamina burden.
